# FORMLORE: Scary Masterpieces collection notes (full text)

> Artworks are public domain; no AI generation or alteration of the artworks. Notes are original FORMLORE writing. Source: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/

## Witch Riding on a Goat

- Artist: Albrecht Dürer
- Date: c. 1500/1501
- Medium: engraving
- Collection: National Gallery of Art, Washington (https://www.nga.gov/collection/art-object-page.6674.html)
- Theme: Witches
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/durer-witch-riding-on-a-goat/

This engraving is barely larger than a playing card, yet it holds a whole sabbath. A witch rides a flying goat backwards, her hair streaming, while putti busy themselves below. Even Dürer's monogram is printed in reverse: the world turned upside down, right down to the signature.

## The Four Witches

- Artist: Albrecht Dürer
- Date: 1497
- Medium: engraving
- Collection: Cleveland Museum of Art (https://www.clevelandart.org/art/1990.85)
- Theme: Witches
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/durer-the-four-witches/

Four nude women stand in a close circle, trading glances that give nothing away, while a devil wreathed in flame and smoke lurks in the doorway at the left. The globe hanging above them carries the letters O.G.H., read as O Gott hüte: God protect us. Dürer engraved it in 1497, and the picture has kept its secret ever since.

## The Witches

- Artist: Hans Baldung Grien
- Date: 1510
- Medium: chiaroscuro woodcut, grey and black
- Collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/336235)
- Theme: Witches
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/baldung-the-witches/

A coven gathers around a jar that erupts into a column of vapour, while one of the witches sails overhead on a flying goat. Baldung printed the design in 1510 from two blocks, a grey tone block beneath the black line block, so the bare paper glows like moonlight. It became one of the defining witch images of the German Renaissance.

## The Bewitched Groom

- Artist: Hans Baldung Grien
- Date: 1544
- Medium: woodcut
- Collection: National Gallery of Art, Washington (https://www.nga.gov/collection/art-object-page.678.html)
- Theme: Witches
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/baldung-the-bewitched-groom/

A stable groom lies sprawled on the floor, foreshortened so steeply that we look straight up the soles of his feet. A horse glances back at him, and a witch with a torch watches from the window. Baldung made the woodcut in 1544, a year before his death, and its meaning is still argued over.

## The Witch of Malleghem

- Artist: Pieter van der Heyden after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
- Date: 1559
- Medium: engraving
- Collection: National Gallery of Art, Washington (https://www.nga.gov/collection/art-object-page.47634.html)
- Theme: Witches
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/heyden-the-witch-of-malleghem/

Bruegel designed it, van der Heyden engraved it and Hieronymus Cock published it in 1559. It is a satire on quackery: a village “witch” cuts the stones of folly from the heads of the gullible while an accomplice crouches inside a giant egg. The joke, five centuries on, still lands.

## The Witch (Night Piece)

- Artist: Jan van de Velde II
- Date: 1626
- Medium: engraving
- Collection: Cleveland Museum of Art (https://www.clevelandart.org/art/1943.635)
- Theme: Witches
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/velde-the-witch-night-piece/

A witch kneels inside her magic circle preparing a brew, surrounded by familiars and the emblems of vice. Van de Velde engraved it in the “dark manner”, carving light out of near-total black. It was made for long nights.

## Witches' Sabbath

- Artist: Jacques de Gheyn II
- Date: late 16th–early 17th century
- Medium: pen and brown ink, brown wash
- Collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/335532)
- Theme: Witches
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/gheyn-witches-sabbath/

Hags crouch around a steaming cauldron, one reaching towards the fire, while an animal prowls at their feet and a plume of smoke rolls overhead. De Gheyn returned to witchcraft again and again, and this sheet has the speed of an artist thinking with the pen. The brownish paper gives the whole scene the colour of smoke.

## Scenes of Witchcraft: Evening

- Artist: Salvator Rosa
- Date: c. 1645–49
- Medium: oil on canvas
- Collection: Cleveland Museum of Art (https://www.clevelandart.org/art/1977.37.3)
- Theme: Witches
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/rosa-scenes-of-witchcraft-evening/

At dusk, hags gather around a cauldron while a conjured skeleton hangs overhead, holding an hourglass. A wax effigy hints at love magic, and the round canvas itself echoes the magic circle. Rosa also wrote verse on the subject. Few paintings are more purely Halloween.

## Scenes of Witchcraft: Night

- Artist: Salvator Rosa
- Date: c. 1645–49
- Medium: oil on canvas
- Collection: Cleveland Museum of Art (https://www.clevelandart.org/art/1977.37.4)
- Theme: Witches
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/rosa-scenes-of-witchcraft-night/

The companion to Evening is darker still. Deep in a forest, a necromancer stands beneath a broken classical column and summons apparitions, while a party of travellers stops to watch from a safe distance. Rosa's learned magicians have been read as a nod to the artist himself and the circle of scholars he kept in Florence.

## Witches Preparing to Fly

- Artist: Francisco de Goya
- Date: 1796/1797
- Medium: brush and ink wash
- Collection: National Gallery of Art, Washington (https://www.nga.gov/collection/art-object-page.73851.html)
- Theme: Witches
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/goya-witches-preparing-to-fly/

In this brush-and-wash drawing, a pig-faced figure rides on the shoulders of a goat-legged one. Two hooded figures in tall conical hats hold a book open with pincers, and a skull waits on the floor. Goya wrote Brujas (witches) beneath it, and a later hand added “a bolar”, to fly. Ideas like this were soon to become his Caprichos.

## The Night-Hag Visiting Lapland Witches

- Artist: Henry Fuseli
- Date: 1796
- Medium: oil on canvas
- Collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/436423)
- Theme: Witches
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/fuseli-the-night-hag-visiting-lapland-witches/

Fuseli took his subject from a simile in Milton's Paradise Lost, in which the night-hag rides the air “lured with the smell of infant blood” to dance with the witches of Lapland while the labouring moon eclipses at their charms. A witch crouches over a pale infant as the hag sweeps in above, lit by an eerie moon. It is the painter of The Nightmare at his most theatrical.

## Macbeth Consulting the Witches

- Artist: Eugène Delacroix
- Date: 1825
- Medium: lithograph
- Collection: Cleveland Museum of Art (https://www.clevelandart.org/art/1962.109)
- Theme: Witches
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/delacroix-macbeth-consulting-the-witches/

Macbeth confronts the witches at their boiling cauldron in this early lithograph. Delacroix worked the stone almost black with greasy crayon, then scratched his design out of the darkness with a sharp point, so the figures seem to surface from smoke. Shakespeare never looked so Romantic.

## Lovers Surprised by Death

- Artist: Hans Burgkmair
- Date: 1510
- Medium: chiaroscuro woodcut
- Collection: Cleveland Museum of Art (https://www.clevelandart.org/art/1952.533)
- Theme: Death
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/burgkmair-lovers-surprised-by-death/

A winged Death seizes a young man while his lover flees, in a setting of canals, gondolas and wide chimney pots that place the scene in Venice. Burgkmair printed it in 1510 from a line block and two tone blocks, the earliest known chiaroscuro woodcut made that way. None of the three blocks tells the story alone; it takes all of them together.

## Dance of Death: The Miser

- Artist: Hans Holbein the Younger
- Date: c. 1526
- Medium: woodcut
- Collection: Cleveland Museum of Art (https://www.clevelandart.org/art/1929.161)
- Theme: Death
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/holbein-dance-of-death-the-miser/

Holbein designed the Dance of Death series and the master block-cutter Hans Lützelburger cut it before his death in 1526. The set was finally published in 1538. Here Death comes for the rich man at his counting table, and no lock or ledger can stop him. The block is tiny but the drama isn't.

## Death and the Miser

- Artist: Hieronymus Bosch
- Date: c. 1485/1490
- Medium: oil on panel
- Collection: National Gallery of Art, Washington (https://www.nga.gov/collection/art-object-page.41645.html)
- Theme: Death
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/bosch-death-and-the-miser/

A dying man sits up in bed as Death, shrouded and holding an arrow, slips through the door. A little demon offers him a bag of gold while an angel turns him towards the crucifix in the window. The panel, probably the wing of a lost altarpiece, is a deathbed lesson drawn from the Ars Moriendi, the art of dying, and even now the miser has not quite chosen.

## The Four Horsemen

- Artist: Albrecht Dürer
- Date: 1498
- Medium: woodcut
- Collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/336215)
- Theme: Death
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/durer-the-four-horsemen/

From Dürer's Apocalypse of 1498, the series of fifteen woodcuts that made his name across Europe. The riders of Revelation thunder from left to right, trampling everyone in their path, with Death in the foreground on a starved and bony nag. Rarely has a block of wood moved so fast.

## Knight, Death, and the Devil

- Artist: Albrecht Dürer
- Date: 1513
- Medium: engraving
- Collection: Cleveland Museum of Art (https://www.clevelandart.org/art/1965.231)
- Theme: Death
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/durer-knight-death-and-the-devil/

One of Dürer's three master engravings. An armoured rider presses on through a rocky gorge, ignoring a horned devil behind him and Death beside him, crowned with snakes and holding up an hourglass. A skull lies underfoot, his dog keeps pace, and the city on the hill is still a long way off.

## The Skeletons

- Artist: Giovanni Battista Piranesi
- Date: 1745–50
- Medium: etching
- Collection: Cleveland Museum of Art (https://www.clevelandart.org/art/1974.253)
- Theme: Death
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/piranesi-the-skeletons/

One of the four Grotteschi that Piranesi etched in the late 1740s, before he became famous for prisons and ruins. Skeletons, tumbled fragments and tangled growth dissolve into a landscape of quick, feathery lines. It reads less like a scene than a fever dream about antiquity.

## Memento Mori, “To This Favour”

- Artist: William Michael Harnett
- Date: 1879
- Medium: oil on canvas
- Collection: Cleveland Museum of Art (https://www.clevelandart.org/art/1965.235)
- Theme: Death
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/harnett-memento-mori-to-this-favour/

A skull, a snuffed candle, a run-down hourglass and a pile of battered books are laid out with almost unnerving realism. Inside one cover Harnett inscribed Hamlet's lines from the graveyard scene: let her paint an inch thick, to this favour she must come. The joke about paint is aimed squarely at the painter's own trompe-l'oeil skill.

## Dance of Death: Death the Strangler

- Artist: Alfred Rethel
- Date: 1850
- Medium: woodcut
- Collection: Cleveland Museum of Art (https://www.clevelandart.org/art/1939.620)
- Theme: Death
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/rethel-dance-of-death-death-the-strangler/

The caption recalls the first outbreak of cholera at a masked ball in Paris in 1831. Death, hooded, saws at a fiddle made of bones while dancers collapse and the musicians flee. Rethel looked back to Holbein and Dürer for this woodcut, and it is every bit as merciless as theirs.

## My Portrait in the Year 1960

- Artist: James Ensor
- Date: 1888
- Medium: etching
- Collection: Cleveland Museum of Art (https://www.clevelandart.org/art/1981.27)
- Theme: Death
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/ensor-my-portrait-in-the-year-1960/

At twenty-eight, Ensor etched himself as a reclining skeleton and dated the portrait seventy-two years ahead. The line is quick and nervous and the joke is very dry: a self-portrait as memento mori.

## Night, from On Death, Part I

- Artist: Max Klinger
- Date: 1889
- Medium: etching and aquatint
- Collection: Cleveland Museum of Art (https://www.clevelandart.org/art/1933.126.1)
- Theme: Death
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/klinger-night-from-on-death-part-i/

The opening plate of Klinger's On Death, Part I, a cycle of ten etchings that one critic called a modern Dance of Death. A man sits alone on a bench in a walled garden as a moonbeam breaks over the sea, while a lily and a butterfly wait on the path. Nothing happens yet, and that is the dread.

## And His Name That Sat on Him Was Death

- Artist: Odilon Redon
- Date: 1899
- Medium: lithograph
- Collection: Cleveland Museum of Art (https://www.clevelandart.org/art/1926.140.3)
- Theme: Death
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/redon-and-his-name-that-sat-on-him-was-death/

This plate comes from The Apocalypse of Saint John, Redon's last lithographic portfolio, published by Ambroise Vollard in 1899. The rider of Revelation is reduced to glare and shadow. It is one of the final great works among Redon's noirs.

## The Race Track (Death on a Pale Horse)

- Artist: Albert Pinkham Ryder
- Date: c. 1896–1908
- Medium: oil on canvas
- Collection: Cleveland Museum of Art (https://www.clevelandart.org/art/1928.8)
- Theme: Death
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/ryder-the-race-track-death-on-a-pale-horse/

The painting grew out of a real loss: a friend of Ryder's staked everything on a horse race, lost, and took his own life. Death rides the empty track with his scythe, and a snake lies in the foreground. Ryder reworked the canvas for years and was reluctant to let it go.

## The Skeleton of the Buses

- Artist: José Guadalupe Posada
- Date: c. 1900–10
- Medium: relief etching and letterpress
- Collection: Cleveland Museum of Art (https://www.clevelandart.org/art/2000.97)
- Theme: Death
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/posada-the-skeleton-of-the-buses/

Posada's calaveras were cheap broadsheets of image and verse, sold on the streets of Mexico City to readers who often could not read the text. Here a tram unloads its passengers straight into a crowd of skulls while Death beckons them on, a comment on the city's dangerous new electric streetcars. The graveyard, it suggests, is simply the last stop.

## The Temptation of Saint Anthony

- Artist: Follower of Pieter Bruegel the Elder
- Date: c. 1550/1575
- Medium: oil on panel
- Collection: National Gallery of Art, Washington (https://www.nga.gov/collection/art-object-page.41602.html)
- Theme: Demons & Temptations
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/bruegel-follower-temptation-of-saint-anthony/

Here the landscape does the talking: a river, a smoking steeple, a giant fish run aground, and creatures riding fish across the sky. Saint Anthony appears twice, once resisting in a rough shelter and once hauled into the air by demons. It rewards a long look.

## The Temptation of Saint Anthony

- Artist: Attributed to Pieter Huys
- Date: 16th century
- Medium: oil on oak
- Collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/436702)
- Theme: Demons & Temptations
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/huys-temptation-of-saint-anthony/

Huys was an Antwerp painter who worked squarely in Bosch's wake, and this panel is a catalogue of borrowed nightmares. The saint, hooded at the left beside his traditional pig, is approached by a nude temptress and a companion bearing a dish, while fires burn on the horizon and hybrid creatures crawl, fly and swim through every corner. It is very nearly five feet wide.

## Christ's Descent into Hell

- Artist: Follower of Hieronymus Bosch
- Date: 16th century
- Medium: oil on wood
- Collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/435725)
- Theme: Demons & Temptations
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/bosch-christ-s-descent-into-hell/

A long, low panel of burning cities, black water and swarming demons, painted by an artist steeped in Bosch's inventions. The subject is Christ's descent to free the souls of the righteous, but the eye goes first to the infernal landscape itself. Look closely: every rock and ruin is occupied.

## The Temptation of Saint Anthony (second version)

- Artist: Jacques Callot
- Date: 1635
- Medium: etching
- Collection: Cleveland Museum of Art (https://www.clevelandart.org/art/2005.179)
- Theme: Demons & Temptations
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/callot-the-temptation-of-saint-anthony-second-version/

Callot etched this second, larger Temptation in 1635, the year of his death, on a plate nearly half a metre wide. A colossal winged demon fills the sky above a swarming theatre of monsters, while the tiny saint holds firm below. Its swarm of invented creatures proved widely influential.

## Satan Starts from the Touch of Ithuriel's Spear

- Artist: Henry Fuseli
- Date: 1776
- Medium: pen and ink, grey wash
- Collection: Cleveland Museum of Art (https://www.clevelandart.org/art/1954.365)
- Theme: Demons & Temptations
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/fuseli-satan-starts-from-the-touch-of-ithuriel-s-spear/

From Milton's Paradise Lost: the angels Ithuriel and Zephon find Satan crouched as a toad beside the sleeping Adam and Eve, and at the touch of Ithuriel's spear he springs back into his true shape. The lion behind recalls an earlier disguise. Fuseli returned to Milton all his life, and this early drawing already crackles.

## The Sleep of Reason Produces Monsters

- Artist: Francisco de Goya
- Date: 1799
- Medium: etching and aquatint
- Collection: National Gallery of Art, Washington (https://www.nga.gov/collection/art-object-page.7502.html)
- Theme: Demons & Temptations
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/goya-the-sleep-of-reason-produces-monsters/

This is plate 43 of Los Caprichos. A man slumps over his desk as owls and bats pour out of the dark behind him, and a lynx-eyed cat keeps watch. The inscription carved into the desk is Goya's whole argument. It is one of the most quoted images in Western art.

## Onoe Matsusuke as the Ghost of Oiwa

- Artist: Utagawa Toyokuni I
- Date: 1812
- Medium: woodblock print, ink and colour
- Collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/45290)
- Theme: Ghosts & Yōkai
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/toyokuni-onoe-matsusuke-as-the-ghost-of-oiwa/

The actor Onoe Matsusuke appears as the vengeful ghost of the murdered wife Oiwa, her long hair loose and her body trailing away into a wisp, ringed by flickering ghost-fire. Ghost plays were a summer staple of the kabuki stage, meant to send a chill through the audience. Toyokuni made the print in 1812.

## Sketch of Ibaraki-dōji

- Artist: Shibata Zeshin
- Date: c. 1840
- Medium: ink on paper, hanging scroll
- Collection: Cleveland Museum of Art (https://www.clevelandart.org/art/1990.6)
- Theme: Ghosts & Yōkai
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/zeshin-sketch-of-ibaraki-doji/

A towering preparatory drawing for a wooden votive plaque, commissioned by a union of wholesalers and offered to a shrine. The demon Ibaraki-dōji reclaims the arm a warrior once cut from him, and the merchants meant it as a prayer: they wanted back the right to sell sugar that the government had taken away. Rarely has a monster been asked to carry a business plan.

## Demons and Monsters

- Artist: Takai Kōzan
- Date: ca. 1870s
- Medium: hanging scroll, ink on paper
- Collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/853220)
- Theme: Ghosts & Yōkai
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/kozan-demons-and-monsters/

Takai Kōzan, a wealthy merchant, scholar and patron of Hokusai, turned in later life to painting yōkai. Here a procession of demons, goblins and grinning monsters tumbles down the scroll in loose, quick ink. It is the night parade as a kind of joyful riot.

## The Hell Courtesan

- Artist: Utagawa Kunisada II
- Date: late 1850s
- Medium: hanging scroll, ink and colour on silk
- Collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/890793)
- Theme: Ghosts & Yōkai
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/kunisada-the-hell-courtesan/

Legend tells of Jigoku-dayū, the Hell Courtesan, who wore robes painted with the torments of hell and became a disciple of the Zen monk Ikkyū. Kunisada II painted her on a tall silk scroll, her robes crowded with scenes of hell. Beauty and damnation, worn as a single garment.

## Island of the Dead

- Artist: Arnold Böcklin
- Date: 1880
- Medium: oil on wood
- Collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/435683)
- Theme: The Crossing
- Page: https://seeeyi.github.io/formlore-site/works/bocklin-island-of-the-dead/

A small boat crosses perfectly still water towards a rocky islet crowded with black cypresses. A figure in white stands at the prow. Böcklin painted this, one of five versions of the subject, in 1880, and it was never really a painting about fear. It is about arriving.
